Prescribed by or in consultation with an indication-appropriate specialist (AD/PN/CSU/BP: allergist/immunologist/dermatologist; asthma: allergist/immunologist/pulmonologist; CRSwNP/EoE: allergist/immunologist/ENT; COPD: pulmonologist).
Atopic Dermatitis: documentation of baseline BSA/severity AND tried/failed or contraindication to at least two of (age-appropriate TCS, topical calcineurin inhibitor, PDE4 inhibitor) for 30 days.
Asthma: eosinophilic phenotype (eos ≥150) OR OCS-dependent; AND ongoing symptoms after ≥3 month ICS+LABA; AND not for acute bronchospasm/status asthmaticus.
CRSwNP: inadequate response/intolerance/CI to a 3-month trial of TWO nasal corticosteroid sprays with different active ingredients; AND used as add-on maintenance.
EoE: ≥15 eos/hpf; dysphagia symptoms; and weight ≥15 kg.
Prurigo Nodularis: baseline BSA/severity documented; AND tried/failed or CI to high-potency corticosteroid ≥30 days.
COPD: inadequate response to triple therapy (LABA+ICS+LAMA) ≥3 months; AND exacerbation history; AND post-BD FEV1/FVC <0.7 with FEV1 30–70% predicted; AND eos ≥300 cells/µL within 60 days.
CSU: urticaria ≥6 weeks with symptoms ≥3 days/week on max-dose non-sedating antihistamine; AND tried/failed or CI to max-dose non-sedating antihistamine ≥60 days.

Bullous Pemphigoid: confirmed by serology or biopsy; BPDAI ≥24 and Peak Pruritus NRS ≥4; failed ≥2 standard therapies (different MOA) ≥1 month each; initially combined with tapering oral corticosteroids.
Denial if used in conjunction with another biologic medication (e.g. Enbrel, Xolair, Remicade).

criteria.text: Indication must be one of the FDA-labeled uses in Alaska Medicaid Xolair PA Criteria: moderate-to-severe persistent asthma, CRSwNP, IgE-mediated food allergy, or chronic spontaneous urticaria (CSU).
Patient meets FDA-labeled age for the requested indication (asthma ≥6y; CSU ≥12y; CRSwNP ≥18y; IgE-mediated food allergy ≥1y).
Prescribed by or in consultation with an indication-appropriate specialist (asthma/CSU/CRSwNP: allergist, immunologist, or pulmonologist; IgE-mediated food allergy: allergist or immunologist).

Asthma: not for acute bronchospasm/status asthmaticus; positive skin or in vitro allergen sensitization; baseline IgE ≥30 IU/mL; inadequately controlled ≥3 months on ICS+LABA, LTRA, theophylline, or oral corticosteroid.

CSU (chronic idiopathic urticaria): urticaria ≥6 weeks with symptoms ≥3 days/week on max-dose non-sedating antihistamine; AND tried/failed or intolerance to leukotriene modifier plus non-sedating antihistamine ≥2 months.
CRSwNP (nasal polyps): baseline serum IgE ≥30 IU/mL; inadequate response/intolerance/CI to a 3-month trial of TWO nasal corticosteroid sprays; AND used as add-on maintenance therapy.
IgE-mediated food allergy: diagnosis confirmed; AND baseline IgE and current weight provided.
Denial if patient is currently using an anti-interleukin 4 or 5 inhibitor.

max_units.notes: AK criteria quantity limits: up to 8 × 150 mg vials per 30 days (max dose 600 mg every 2 or 4 weeks); 2 × 75 mg vials per 30 days. Approval up to 3 months; reauthorization up to 12 months.

notes: Partial encoding from AK Xolair criteria PDF (Version 3, original 02/28/2020, approval 9/16/2022, update 04/19/2024, effective 06/1/2024).

Not encoded as numeric predicates (attestation only): exact IgE IU/mL, body weight kg, vial quantity math, anaphylaxis-setting/malignancy/serum-sickness cautions.
